guide.title: Mozart: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, K. 525 – IV. Rondo (Allegro): A Listening Guide
guide.overview: This movement is a rondo for string quartet. A rondo is a piece where the main tune keeps coming back. The home key is G major. Listen for the opening tune in the first violin, and for how it returns in other keys and then in G major. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so small details may be off. The score has no loudness markings, so the guide says little about loud and soft.

listening_points.headline: The main tune opens in the first violin
listening_points.text: The movement starts with the first violin playing the main tune [m. 0-2]. In the first measure only the first violin plays, so it is alone. The others then join as accompaniment. The tune comes back a few bars later [m. 4-6]. This opening part is repeated.

listening_points.headline: Part 2 begins, still in G major
listening_points.text: A new part starts [m. 10]. It begins with the parts moving together in chords. The viola probably takes the tune for a moment [m. 11-12], though the lead is uncertain there. At [m. 14] the parts play in unison or octaves, meaning they play the same notes. The analysis marks this as its loudest or busiest point, but that is only a computer estimate.

listening_points.headline: The music moves through D major and A major
listening_points.text: The key moves to D major [m. 15]. Around [m. 19-20] the texture is a trio, so three parts are playing. Then the key moves to A major [m. 23]. The first violin probably leads most of this stretch, but the estimate is not very sure.

listening_points.headline: The main tune returns in D major
listening_points.text: The key returns to D major [m. 32]. The first violin plays the main tune again, five semitones lower than at the start [m. 32-34]. It plays it once more [m. 36-38]. This is the familiar tune in a new key.

listening_points.headline: Other instruments step forward
listening_points.text: The lead passes around. The cello probably leads for a while [m. 41-43]. Then the second violin probably shares the tune with the first violin [m. 44-46]. The lead estimate is low here, so think of it as shared.

listening_points.headline: Part 2 winds down toward C major
listening_points.text: The parts move together in chords [m. 47-49]. Then the first violin leads over accompaniment [m. 50-55]. The key briefly shifts to C major at the end of the part [m. 56a-57b]. The cello probably has the lead at [m. 57b]. This part is repeated.

listening_points.headline: Part 3 turns to C minor and E-flat major
listening_points.text: Part 3 opens in unison or octaves [m. 58]. The key is C minor [m. 58-60]. The cello plays a close echo of the main tune, two octaves lower [m. 57b-60]. The first violin plays the tune in C minor [m. 59-61]. It plays it again in E-flat major [m. 63-65].

listening_points.headline: A long stretch in G minor
listening_points.text: The key changes to G minor [m. 71-74]. The first violin leads, and the others accompany. A brief touch of G major appears [m. 75-76]. Then G minor returns [m. 77-83]. In [m. 81-82] the parts play in unison or octaves.

listening_points.headline: D major and G major return
listening_points.text: The key moves to D major [m. 84-86]. Then G major arrives [m. 87-91], with a trio texture of three parts at first [m. 87-88]. D major returns [m. 92-99].

listening_points.headline: The main tune is back in G major
listening_points.text: The first violin plays the main tune at its original pitch [m. 100-102]. It plays it again, one octave lower [m. 104-106]. The others accompany.

listening_points.headline: The lead is passed around again
listening_points.text: The cello probably leads first [m. 109-111]. Then the second violin probably leads [m. 112-114]. The first violin probably takes over with the parts moving together in chords [m. 115-117]. The lead estimates here are low, so the lead is best heard as shared.

listening_points.headline: A detour through F major and C major
listening_points.text: The key moves to F major [m. 123-127]. Then it moves to C major [m. 128-131]. The parts mostly move together in chords. A unison or octave moment appears at [m. 125] and again at [m. 131], where Part 4 begins.

listening_points.headline: The main tune returns in G major again
listening_points.text: Part 4 begins with the first violin playing the main tune at the opening pitch [m. 132-134]. It plays it again at [m. 136-138]. The key stays in G major while the first violin leads over accompaniment.

listening_points.headline: One more visit to D major
listening_points.text: The key moves to D major [m. 147-153]. The second violin probably takes the lead from [m. 149]. From [m. 150] the parts play independent lines, so each has its own melody.

listening_points.headline: G major to the end
listening_points.text: The key is G major again from [m. 154]. The first violin probably leads over accompaniment [m. 157-162]. The parts move together in chords at [m. 163-164]. The last measure is in unison or octaves [m. 165].

glossary.explanation: A piece where the main tune keeps coming back between other music.
The home note and scale that a passage feels centered on.
A change from one key to another.
Instruments play the same notes, at the same pitch or in different octaves.
The parts move together in chords, with the same rhythm.
One part has the tune and the others support it.
Three parts are active at once.
Each part plays its own melodic line.
